=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21886-21891 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Old exit 1 guards coexist with the new rb_fix_scope_check call at line 21894. When ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false, the grep-based guard at line 21886 fires exit(1) before rb_fix_scope_check ever runs. This means the structured rejection path (REVIEW_BLOCKED_FIX_SCOPE_REJECTED logging, tg_notify WARNING, REVIEW_BLOCKED_STATE_CHANGED=true, retry counting) is never reached. The poller silently exits instead of going through the intended scope-rejection reporting pipeline.
  WHY: The old guards at lines 21886-21891 preempt the rb_fix_scope_check call at 21894. The LAST RUN DIFF removed these guards and replaced them with a single staging step followed by rb_fix_scope_check, but both old and new code paths remain in the file. The old path also exits with exit(1) while the new path consumes a retry and alerts operators. An `exit 1` halfway through a larger shell function can leave stale worktrees and unposted state comments.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21866-21882 (old conditional staging) coexisting with line 21877 (new simplified staging) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The file retains both the old conditional staging block (if ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true then add X; else add Y) and the new simplified add. When ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true, both the simplified add (21877) and the old exit guards fire, but the staged file set is the same from both paths, so the effect is benign aside from the dead code. When ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false, the old else branch stages only non-protected files (excluding scripts, prompts, .github/ai, .github/workflows) and then the old grep guard at 21886 fires exit(1). The rb_fix_scope_check path was designed to stage everything and then check the scope, but the old conditional prevents protected files from ever reaching the scope check.
  WHY: The intended flow stages all files, then scope-checks, then either commits or rejects with reporting. The old staging excludes protected files before the scope check can reject them with the structured path, making the scope guard operate on an incomplete staged set.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:9734-9742 (test_review_blocked_fix_scope_rejects_empty_staged_set) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF shows this test was updated to use touch=".github/prompts/excluded.txt" (a path excluded from staging, producing an empty staged set) and a separate test_review_blocked_fix_scope_rejects_workflow_edit_opt_out was added. On disk, neither change landed: the empty-staged test still uses scripts/excluded.sh with ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false (which the old guards would intercept before the scope check), and the workflow-edit-opt-out test does not exist.
  WHY: The test coverage for the new workflow_edits_disabled rejection path is absent. If the scope guard were to be fixed, the ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false rejection path has no test coverage confirming it logs REJECTED, does not push, and consumes a retry.

  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF added documentation explaining that when ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false, edits to scripts/, prompts/, .github/ai/, or .github/workflows/ reject the entire fix through the retry path. These documentation lines are absent from both README.md and agents.md.
  WHY: Operators who set ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false have no documented explanation of the rejection behavior, only the old guards which silently exit without retry counting or alerts.

  WHY: Without this loop, rb_fix_scope_check lacks the early-reject capability for forbidden artifacts and workflow-edit opt-out. The ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false case is handled only by the old exit 1 guard which preempts the whole function.
